question.problem:
Let $\mathbf{X} = [X_1,X_2]^T$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y = 3X_1 + X_2 .$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $\mathbf{X} = [X_1, X_2]^T$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y= aX_1 + bX_2
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $\mu_1 = 2$ and $\mu_2 = -1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[3{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}] \\  & =3\text{E}[{X}_{1}]+\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & =3\cdot {\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2} \\  & =3\cdot 2+(-1) \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have $\sigma_1^2 = 4, \sigma_2^2 = 7,$ and $\sigma_{12} = \sigma_{21} = -3.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[3{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}] \\  & ={3}^{2}\cdot 4+{1}^{2}\cdot 7+2\cdot 3\cdot 1\cdot (-3) \\  & =36+7-18 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y \sim N(5,25).
$$
